answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit orders or earn rewards. A registry ties the stake to a persistent key, and conflicting reports or proven double-spending trigger forfeiture; reputation then accrues per unit of stake and time, not per account. This makes one anchor for each identity costly to multiply: a sybil attacker must immobilize more capital and risks losing it, while a canyon of cheap fabricated accounts gains no extra weight. Honest participation can return nectar as fees or rewards.
